_doc: W316 — DECLARED EXCEPTIONS TO THE TENANT SCOPE FENCE.
An entry here is INERT ON ITS OWN. The fence requires BOTH this entry AND a
'/* TENANT-SCOPE-EXEMPT: <key> */' marker immediately above the statement it
excuses. A marker with no entry FAILS the build ('an undeclared exception'),
and an entry with no marker FAILS the build as STALE ('an exception that
outlived the code it excused'). Two places, both required, both checked in
both directions — because a one-place exception list is how a fence quietly
'ruling' must name the authority that decided the read may cross tenants.
'countervailingControl' must name what keeps the exception honest: an
exception with nothing standing against it is an unbounded permission.

exemptions.ruling: Owner ruling Q10 — the cohort benchmark MUST STAY CROSS-TENANT.
reason: A benchmark computed inside one tenant is not a benchmark. It compares a
GP's portfolio to itself and returns approximately 1.00 by construction,
which is worse than no number: it looks like a peer comparison and is not
one. The whole product value of this read is that the cohort spans the
platform.
No individual subject's figures are disclosed by it: the read returns one
aggregate, gated on 'benchmark.min_cohort_n' so a cohort small enough to
re-identify a member is refused outright.
countervailingControl: WAVE 221 (R190.10) — subjects who opt out of benchmarking are filtered
OUT WHERE THE NUMBER IS MADE, in this same function, not at display time.
shared/wave221BenchmarkingOptOutCopy.ts carries the user-facing copy and
exemptions.provenAfterChange: server/__tests__/w316_cross_tenant_reporting_scope.test.ts asserts this read STILL returns a cohort assembled from more than one tenant after W316.

exemptions.ruling: Owner question Q-D, delegated and decided in W316: DO NOT SCOPE THIS READ. W303 explicitly protected the '/api/me/**' surface.
reason: This read is IDENTITY-scoped, which is TIGHTER than tenant-scoped, not
looser: 'WHERE lp_id IN (resolveInvestorIdSet(canonicalUserId))' returns
only rows belonging to the caller themselves.
Adding a tenant predicate here would REMOVE ROWS THE LP LEGITIMATELY OWNS.
An LP who has committed to vehicles under two different GPs owns cashflows
under two tenant ids; scoping '/api/me/cashflows' to one of them would
silently drop half of their own distributions from their own DPI. That is
not a smaller leak — it is a WRONG NUMBER on the investor's own statement.
Re-verified in W316 by reading the SQL and censusing the call sites: one
production caller, server/lib/reportingEngineRoutes.ts, route
GET /api/me/cashflows. The exclusion in the specification HELD.
countervailingControl: single decider of which ids denote the caller, and an empty set returns [],
never an unfiltered read. The route sits behind the authenticated /api/me
surface, so lp_id is derived from the session and never from the request.
exemptions.provenAfterChange: server/__tests__/w316_cross_tenant_reporting_scope.test.ts drives GET /api/me/cashflows as a CONTROL and asserts it still returns the LP's own cross-tenant rows.

exemptions.ruling: Owner question Q-E, delegated and decided in W316: derive the tenant from the caller's own holdings.
reason: This is the read that DERIVES the tenant scope, so it cannot itself be
tenant-scoped — there is nothing to scope it to yet. Requiring a tenant
here would be circular.
It is instead scoped by the caller's own identity, with the SAME predicate
'investorHoldsCompany' already trusts to authorise the request:
investor_id = caller, company_id = the company in the path,
state = 'committed', deleted_at IS NULL. It reads no figure of any kind —
only the DISTINCT tenant ids of the caller's own committed holdings.
server/lib/userContext.ts, which would otherwise be the place to carry a
tenant id, is FROZEN this wave and carries none.
countervailingControl: Fails CLOSED: an unreadable table, a thrown query, or a blank tenant_id
yields an empty array, and GET /api/investor/portfolio/:id/marks turns an
empty scope into the same byte-identical 404 it already returns for 'you do
not hold this company'. It cannot widen a read.
asTenantScope() refuses an empty scope, so 'scope to nothing' — which would
return an empty chart to everyone and pass a naive leak test — is not
